edge_board.description: The 60-day negotiation window established by the June 2026 Islamabad Memorandum between the United States and Iran approaches its mid-August deadline amid stalled direct talks and competing mediation efforts. Recent developments include Iranian denials of active bilateral negotiations, U.S. statements emphasizing ongoing diplomacy via Oman and Qatar on Strait of Hormuz access, and mixed progress on nuclear transparency and sanctions relief. Vice President Vance noted talks would prove lengthy and complex, while President Trump described the period as a final opportunity for agreement. These factors, combined with the absence of a finalized deal on enrichment limits or asset releases, underpin trader consensus around a modest likelihood of mutual extension to sustain the ceasefire framework.
edge_board.question: US-Iran 60 day negotiation period extended?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
On June 14, 2026, the United States and Iran announced a written diplomatic agreement (the MOU), including a 60-day negotiation period toward a “final deal”, extendable by mutual consent.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if both the United States and Iran publicly and officially announce an extension of the 60-day negotiation period initiated by the MOU between market creation and August 20, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying announcement must be a declarative statement of a present extension of the 60-day negotiation period, a previously-unannounced prior extension of the 60-day negotiation period, or definitive agreement to extend the 60-day negotiation period.

A qualifying announcement must clearly and unambiguously identify an extension of the 60-day negotiation period initiated by the MOU. Statements that merely allude to, reference, or describe an extension, without clearly communicating it, do not qualify. However, the announcement need not use specific terminology or reference the MOU by name.

A qualifying announcement must be made through official channels, by an individual acting in an official capacity. Statements made incidentally or informally in a context not intended for official communication do not qualify.

The extension must be mutually announced by the United States and the Islamic Republic of Iran by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Mutual announcement means that taken together, the announcements from the United States and the Islamic Republic of Iran directly indicate that both parties have agreed to extend the 60-day negotiation period, or have recognized a definitive extension of the period.

The following do not qualify as official announcements: 
- Anonymous, unattributed, or leaked statements not confirmed as official; 
- Statements by persons not authorized to speak for the United States or Iran;
- Third-party speculation, analysis, or predictions that the United States or Iran will announce or implement an extension of the 60-day negotiation period; 
- Satirical, fabricated, hacked, or impersonated communications; 
- Statements that describe a prospective, contingent, probable, or conditional extension of the 60-day negotiation period rather than announcing a present and decided position.

Once an extension has been mutually announced by the United States and Iran, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether it is later reversed, or whether the extension is ever actually implemented.

Resolution will be based on official information from the United States and Iran, including their official representatives.

edge_board.description: The current 67% market-implied probability for No reflects traders' assessment that another nine-figure sale at or above $150 million is unlikely before year-end, even after the strong May 2026 results from the S.I. Newhouse collection. Jackson Pollock’s “Number 7A” fetched $181.2 million and Constantin Brâncuși’s “Danaïde” reached $107.6 million at Christie’s, confirming robust demand for blue-chip modern works. However, subsequent auctions have lacked comparable fresh-to-market masterpieces, with top lots clustering in the $80–110 million range. The fall season offers limited high-end supply, and no announced consignments suggest a repeat outlier. Historical patterns show such thresholds are crossed only sporadically, supporting trader consensus around the current odds while leaving room for late-year momentum shifts.
edge_board.question: Will an artwork sell for $150 million by December 31?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any single lot is sold at public auction for an all-in price (inclusive of buyer's premium) of at least $150 million at a major auction house between market creation and December 31, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a major auction house will be one of the following: Sotheby's. Christie's, or Phillips. If no such lot is reported by December 31, 2026, 11:59PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve according to the official post-sales results as published on each auction house's official website. If the resolution source becomes permanently unavailable or no qualifying report is released by December 31, 2026, 11:59PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

edge_board.description: Heightened tensions from the ongoing US-Israel-Iran conflict, including renewed military activity in July 2026, continue to shape trader assessments of potential Israeli airspace closures. Israeli authorities have closed and reopened the Tel Aviv FIR multiple times earlier in 2026 amid Iranian missile and drone responses to strikes. As of early August, civil aviation remains operational with Ben-Gurion Airport functioning normally, though EASA maintains advisories on elevated risks and the US Embassy issued an August 1 alert citing possible short-notice disruptions. Diplomats and military statements are closely watched for signs of escalation that could trigger temporary restrictions before key deadlines.
edge_board.question: Israel closes its airspace by August 15?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Israel initiates a major closure of its airspace by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

A “major closure” is defined as a broad closure, cancellation, or complete suspension of commercial aviation across the entirety of Israeli civilian airspace or a region encompassing a majority of Israeli civilian airspace, including commercial flights transiting, arriving in, and departing from that airspace. A qualifying closure must apply generally to all flights across Israel or a qualifying subset of Israeli airspace. Limited cancellations, delays, temporary ground stops or isolated regional closures will not qualify. Limited exceptions to a broad closure, however, will not disqualify such a closure from counting (e.g. exceptions for certain pre-approved flights may be permitted).

Warnings, No-Fly-Zones, flight suspensions, or other flight restrictions imposed by airlines or countries other than Israel will not be sufficient for a “Yes” resolution.

Airspace closures which occur solely due to weather conditions will not qualify.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Israeli aviation authorities; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

edge_board.description: Recent inflation data and a resilient labor market have kept the federal funds rate at 3.50–3.75% through July 2026, with market-implied odds near 54.5% for at least one 25-basis-point hike by year-end. Persistent price pressures, including energy costs tied to geopolitical factors, and solid employment growth have prompted three FOMC dissents favoring tighter policy, while June CPI cooled to 3.5% year-over-year and core measures eased toward 2.6%. Fed funds futures now price rates near 4% by December. The closely balanced sentiment reflects uncertainty over whether July employment and CPI releases on August 12, alongside the September FOMC meeting, will confirm durable disinflation or reinforce the need for restrictive monetary policy to anchor expectations.
edge_board.question: Fed rate hike in 2026?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is increased at any point between January 1, 2026 and the Fed's December 2026 meeting, currently scheduled for December 8-9, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This market may not resolve to "No" until the Fed has released its rate change decision following its December meeting.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official website of the Federal Reserve (https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm), however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

edge_board.question: Will any company announce that it has achieved Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) before Oct 1, 2026?
edge_board.resolution_criteria: If any company (public or private) officially announces that it has achieved Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) after market issuance and before Oct 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes. To qualify, the announcement must explicitly state that the company has achieved, attained, reached, or developed Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), or that it has achieved, attained, reached, or developed “AGI.” Statements that describe “AGI-like,” “AGI-level,” “near-AGI,” or “toward AGI” systems without explicitly stating that the company has achieved/attained/reached/developed AGI do not qualify. For purposes of this market, a “company” includes any publicly traded company or any privately held company whose existence and corporate identity is verifiable and whose financing/valuation or corporate profile is covered by at least two of the listed major business news sources.

edge_board.description: Kai Cenat and IShowSpeed launched their Minecraft Hardcore marathon on August 7, 2026, committing to a nonstop stream until they defeat the Ender Dragon, Wither, Elder Guardian, and Warden without dying. The permadeath rules and multi-boss requirements create high failure risk, echoing their prior 106-hour run that ended in repeated deaths. Trader sentiment reflects this difficulty, with low implied odds for completion by mid-August driven by the need for coordinated resource gathering, precise combat, and endurance across extended sessions. Recent Day 1 streams drew millions of views, while expert commentary highlights the challenge's potential to drag on indefinitely absent major breakthroughs in strategy or luck. Key near-term catalysts include ongoing live progress and any reported deaths that reset attempts.
edge_board.question: Will Kai and Speed beat the Minecraft challenge by August 17?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
Kai Cenat and IShowSpeed are scheduled to stream a hardcore Minecraft marathon on August 7, 2026, at 5:00 PM ET. They will attempt a challenge to defeat the Ender Dragon, the Wither, the Warden, and the Elder Guardian in a hardcore Minecraft world on Java Edition, on the same seed, without either player dying in-game. 

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Kai and Speed complete the aforementioned challenge live on stream between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

All four objectives must be completed on the same seed and in the same world. Progress across multiple seeds will not be combined.

Any successful attempt within the specified timeframe will qualify; however, no challenge progress may be carried over following an in-game death and the beginning of a new attempt. 

Practice or casual worlds not set to Hardcore will not count. No event will count if it occurs while the player in question is in Creative or Spectator mode, or if it results from the use of commands, cheats, or any external tool to spawn entities, alter the world, or deal damage.

Only completion of the challenge as defined above will qualify. If Kai and Speed modify the rules of the challenge at any point, including by removing an objective, adding a player, or playing outside of Hardcore mode, any completion achieved under the modified rules will not count toward resolution.

Only events occurring while at least one of the two players is broadcasting the challenge live will count. Footage of off-stream or previously recorded attempts will not qualify.

If the challenge is cancelled by, abandoned before completion by, or delayed to a point after the specified date, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be footage from the official broadcasts of the challenge on Kai Cenat's and IShowSpeed's official broadcasts on YouTube and Twitch.

edge_board.description: Recent developments center on fragile diplomacy over the Strait of Hormuz and lingering effects of the 2026 Iran conflict. A two-week ceasefire took effect in April 2026, followed by a June memorandum of understanding that aimed to restore navigation, ease sanctions, and address Iran's nuclear program within a 60-day window. Low-intensity clashes resumed in July after Iranian attacks on shipping prompted U.S. strikes and a renewed blockade, with President Trump declaring the truce over. As of early August 2026, U.S., Iranian, and Omani officials are nearing an interim Hormuz access agreement that could restart broader talks, while Trump has signaled optimism about a near-term end to hostilities. Key variables include compliance with navigation rules, enforcement of any new pause, and parallel nuclear or sanctions negotiations.

edge_board.description: **No change leads at 62.5%** because the FOMC held rates at the 3.5–3.75% range in its July 29 decision by a 9-3 vote amid elevated inflation and solid labor conditions, with the majority preferring to await fresh July and August CPI and employment data before the mid-September meeting. Persistent core PCE inflation near 3.3% and headline pressures from recent oil-price spikes tied to Middle East tensions have kept hawkish concerns alive, supporting the 34.5% odds on a 25-basis-point hike. Markets assign negligible probability to cuts because employment remains near maximum-employment levels and inflation has not yet returned to the 2% target. The September outcome will hinge on whether incoming inflation prints show sustained energy-driven upside or begin to moderate.
edge_board.question: Will there be no change in Fed interest rates after the September 2026 meeting?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's September 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for September 15-16, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their September meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

edge_board.description: Ongoing geopolitical tensions from the U.S.-Iran conflict have kept daily transits through the Strait of Hormuz at 9–16 vessels recently versus the pre-2026 average of 60–100, severely constraining flows that account for roughly 20–25% of global seaborne crude and significant LNG volumes. This has supported elevated energy prices and prompted rerouting costs while traders monitor Iran-Oman negotiations over a safe shipping corridor announced in early August. Recent AIS data show only marginal improvement despite earlier cease-fire signals, with insurance premiums and security risks continuing to limit tanker participation. Key near-term catalysts include further diplomatic progress and any verifiable uptick in PortWatch-measured arrivals that could shift market-implied odds on normalization timelines.
edge_board.question: Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by August 31?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Strait of Hormuz equal to or above 60 for any date between market creation and August 31, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Daily transit calls include container, dry bulk, roll-on/roll-off, general cargo, and tanker ships. Ships not reported by IMF Portwatch will not be considered.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls equal to or above the specified level, or once data has been published for the final date in the specified period and no such value has been published. If no data has been published for the final date of the specified period within 14 calendar days (ET) after the end of that period, this market will resolve based on data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points made within this market’s timeframe will be considered. However, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions to previously published data points after data is published for August 31, 2026, however, will not be considered.

In case of obvious data integrity issues (i.e., erroneous data), the market may remain open until the end of the third calendar day (ET) after the date on which such data is first released to allow for corrections. Data integrity issues refer only to clerical or other similar errors in the underlying data, and do not include cases where IMF Portwatch differs from alternative sources.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF Portwatch, specifically the transit calls data published for the Strait of Hormuz at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/cb5856222a5b4105adc6ee7e880a1730, both in the chart and through downloadable files.

This view aligns with the absence of visible amphibious mobilization, naval logistics buildup, or air and maritime surges that would precede an invasion attempt in the narrow window remaining before December 31, 2026. Routine PLA drills and vessel activity in the Taiwan Strait reflect ongoing gray-zone tactics rather than imminent offensive preparations, while Taiwan continues resilience-focused exercises. Trader consensus at 96% for no invasion captures these structural barriers, including high operational risks and economic costs. Late diplomatic crises or internal leadership shifts could theoretically alter trajectories, though such developments would still face significant logistical and strategic hurdles.
edge_board.question: Will China invade Taiwan by end of 2026?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China commences a military offensive intended to establish control over any portion of the Republic of China (Taiwan) by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Territory under the administration of the Republic of China including any inhabited islands will qualify, however uninhabited islands will not qualify. 

The resolution source for this market will be will be official confirmation by China, Taiwan, the United Nations, or any permanent member of the UN Security Council, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.
